questions: How are the two client C_BaseViewModel instances associated with models, weapons, sequence state and the player camera?
Which gates control submission and which client animation events are visual only?

functions.label: base_viewmodel_set_weapon
functions.role: store the associated client weapon EHANDLE

functions.label: base_viewmodel_apply_model
functions.role: apply received model state and reset interpolation parity

functions.label: base_viewmodel_fire_event
functions.role: offer a client animation event to the associated weapon then run visual fallback effects

functions.label: calc_viewmodel_view
functions.role: seed a viewmodel root from the player view origin and angles

functions.label: calc_view
functions.role: update both viewmodel slots each frame

functions.label: setup_view
functions.role: write world and viewmodel FOV and clip planes

functions.label: should_draw_viewmodel
functions.role: apply model, camera, entity, cvar and player-visibility gates

functions.label: draw_viewmodels

functions.role: build each submitted viewmodel model's independent bone palette

relationships.evidence: the draw loop gates each slot before submission
FireEvent resolves the associated client weapon before offering the event hook

findings.fact: Each C_BaseViewModel owns its received model, sequence, cycle and bone evaluation; both are rooted from the same player view and independently submitted in the same dedicated pass.
findings.evidence: CalcView 0x10191200 updates slots 0 and 1 through CalcViewModelView 0x10190ba0; DrawViewModels 0x10198fa0 loops the same two slots, applies ShouldDrawViewModel and submits each renderable, which reaches its own SetupBones.
findings.consequence: The models align by the common camera root and compatible baked skeleton space, not by attaching a weapon component to a hand mesh at runtime.

findings.fact: C_BaseViewModel::FireEvent is a client visual-event consumer and has no authoritative ammunition or damage path.
findings.evidence: 0x100ab530 first offers the event to the associated client weapon hook and otherwise handles attachment effects before the generic client animation-event fallback; the server shot body is in vampire.dll.
findings.consequence: Muzzle flash and magazine events may drive presentation, but never commit a shot or reload transaction.

findings.fact: Viewmodel visibility is gated by the caller flag, model presence, first/third-person and observer state, entity drawing, r_drawviewmodel, engine broadcast state, internal draw policy, player-body visibility state and current view entity.
findings.evidence: ShouldDrawViewModel 0x10198ea0 contains the complete ordered predicate chain and has one caller in DrawViewModels.
findings.consequence: DrawViewmodel has scoped lifetime as a per-view decision; it does not destroy either viewmodel entity or clear its animation state.
